input.question: Which educational institution did Radionova Nataliya Vasilievna attend?

documents.text: As Nataliya Vasilievna Radionova delved deeper into the mysteries of the Amazonian rainforest, the humid air clung to her skin like a damp shroud. The Ukrainian biologist had always been drawn to the uncharted territories of the natural world, and her latest research project had brought her to the heart of Brazil. It was the early 1970s, and the University of São Paulo was abuzz with intellectual fervor, its corridors thrumming with the energy of curious minds. Nataliya, with her wild curls and piercing green eyes, stood out among the sea of students, her Eastern European accent a gentle melody amidst the Portuguese chatter. She had arrived at the university seeking answers to the questions that had haunted her since her childhood in Kiev: What secrets lay hidden in the intricate web of life? How did the delicate balance of ecosystems sustain themselves? As she navigated the sprawling campus, Nataliya found herself drawn to the charismatic Professor Oliveira, whose lectures on tropical ecology were as captivating as they were challenging. His words painted vivid pictures of the forest floor, where towering trees stretched towards the sky and the rustle of leaves concealed a world of hidden wonders. Nataliya's fascination with the subject matter was matched only by her admiration for the professor's infectious enthusiasm. One fateful evening, as the sun dipped below the horizon, Nataliya found herself invited to join Professor Oliveira's research team on an expedition into the depths of the rainforest. The prospect of venturing into the unknown, surrounded by the sights, sounds, and scents of the Amazon, was too enticing to resist. And so, with her backpack loaded with notebooks, cameras, and an insatiable curiosity, Nataliya set off into the heart of Brazil, her Ukrainian roots momentarily forgotten in the face of her all-consuming passion for discovery.
